- Highlights

      - Added Parquet and Avro encryption support (Thanks, Gidon!)
      - Added Spark support for reading, dropping, renaming views (Thanks, Eduard!)
      - Added initial setup for Kafka Connect (Thanks, Bryan!)
      - Added Spark support for delete file granularity (Thanks, Anton!)
      - Removed support for Spark 3.2 (Thanks, Ajantha!)
      - Parallelized file footer reads in add_files procedure (Thanks, Manu!)
      - Docs: Updated new docs to look like the existing docs (Thanks, Bits!)
      - PyIceberg

          - Added write support in PyIceberg (Thanks, Fokko!)
          - Added commit support for PyIceberg Hive (Thanks, Kevin!)
          - Added commit support for SQL catalog (Thanks, Sung!)
          - Added Parquet name mapping support in PyIceberg (Thanks, Sung!)
      - Rust: Added expressions and basic scan planning (Thanks, Renjie!)

          - <https://rust.iceberg.apache.org/>
  - Releases

      - Docs refactor (Bits)

          - Relevant email thread: <https://lists.apache.org/thread/dv2x9n6pkykmstkhrw1fx934qjtxnofy>
          - Docs: <https://github.com/apache/iceberg/tree/main/site>
          - Need votes, will aim to do cutover prior to 1.5.0 and manual release
      - Java 1.5.0 ([milestone](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/milestone/37))

          - Kafka Connect
          - CREATE VIEW
          - Default values in copy-on-write MERGE (Spark 3.4)
          - View support on JDBC, Hive, REST, …
      - Python 0.6.0

          - <https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/milestone/1>
          - Write support
  - Discussion

      - Spatial extensions to Iceberg

          - Prior art: [Geoparquet](https://github.com/opengeospatial/geoparquet), [Geoarrow](https://github.com/geoarrow/geoarrow), [Havasu](https://github.com/wherobots/havasu/)
          - [WKB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well-known_text_representation_of_geometry#Well-known_binary) - Well integrated, not the most performant/space considerate
          - Better performance would be closer to geoarrow, but will be less familiar to developers and anyone trying to integrate with Geo format
          - How do we actually store these we will dive into in a follow up discussion facilitated on the dev list.

body:
([Meeting Recording](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9TRhgRq5bFk) ⭕)

- Highlights

      - New issue template for spec and design proposals (Thanks, Dan!)
      - Added support for manifest encryption (Thanks, Gidon!)
      - Fixed function pushdown for row-level commands in Spark (Thanks, Anton!)
      - Added support for output spec selection in rewrite data files (Thanks, Himadri!)
      - Iceberg-rust:

          - We have added hive catalog support(except update table methods). Thanks Xuanwo and Marvin Lanhenke(github id: marvinlanhenke)!
          - The glue catalog is in progress. Thanks Marvin Lanhenke(github id: marvinlanhenke)!
          - Some enhancement of rest catalog, such as oauth, custom headers. Thanks whynick1, TennyZhuang, Himadri Pal(himadripal)!
          - The community is actively working on reading support, including reading to arrow, filter support, please stay tuned!
          - We have more and more contributors involved in the development, and the number of contributors has reached 36!
          - I have created a github project to help schedule the development so that contributors could easily pick up issues they are interested in!
  - Releases

      - 1.5.0 is released!
      - 1.5.1

          - Branch schemas with time travel reads
          - Trino: extra HEAD request through S3FileIO
          - JDBC Catalog: FIx Escape character in GetNamespace SQL
      - 1.6.0

          - Arrow 16: CVE fixes
      - PyIceberg 0.6.1 - [0.6.1 milestone](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/milestone/5?closed=1)

          - [#544](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/pull/544)
  - Discussion

      - Spec and design proposals

          - New issue template
      - REST protocol evolution and adding new capabilities ([#9940](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/9940))
      - Schema behavior with time travel reads and refs (behavior changed with [#9131](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/9131) to return the table’s schema for branches and the snapshot’s schema for tags)
      - Flink table maintenance - Working on this feature, any input is welcome

          - Continuous streaming jobs

              - Quick compaction for small files and manifest files
              - Periodic orphan file removal
              - Periodic snapshot expiration
          - Scheduled by Flink SinkV2 PostCommitTopology and/or Monitor
          - RewriteFileGroupPlanner - refactored out from Spark to common
          - RollingManifestWriter - enhancement for streaming
      - Catalog discussion – on hold

          - Deprecate DynamoDB catalog ([thread](https://lists.apache.org/thread/b92zwcvy7917bhr5t00b07f7r8qqwxqj))
      - Problem with Iceberg [Spark 3.3 & 3.5 merge into](https://apache-iceberg.slack.com/archives/C025PH0G1D4/p1695858665345709)

          - with source and target both as an iceberg table, merge into is resulting in full table loads of the Target table when partitioned with Hash bucketing.
          - The problem is that DPP is not kicking in.

()

- Highlights

      - Specs

          - Agreed on spec changes for Row lineage (Thanks, Russell!)

      - Java

          - Added interfaces for rewrite table path actions ([#10920](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/10920)) (Thanks, Laith!)
          - Updated AWS to use base-2 entropy (Thanks, Ozan and Drew!)
          - Updated credential passing in loadTable (Thanks, Eduard!)

          - Spark: updated to auto-compact deletes (Thanks, Anton!)
      - Rust

      - PyIceberg

          - Added metadata table for data_files and delete_files (Thanks Soumya!)
          - Added flag to allow users to disable the creation of tables on SqlCatalog initialization (Thanks Patrick!)
      - Go

          - Iceberg schema/types conversion to Arrow (Thanks, Matt)
          - Arrow type promotion (Thanks, Matt)
          - Improvements to Glue catalog (Thanks, natusioe)
          - Better config file handling (Thanks, Alex)
      - Releases

          - 1.7.0

              - Release Cutoff Date for 1.7

                  - Get code in by the end of the week please
                  - Need to check licenses on connector and on REST Test binaries
              - Do potential Release on Oct 31st to be brought up on dev list
      - Discussion

          - **[Partial Table Metadata Retriev](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eXnT0ZiFvdm_Zvk6fLGT_UxVWO-HsiqVywqu1Uk8s7E/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.uad1lm906wz4)al**
              - **Problem : Metadata is growing quite large, Metadata is being transferred between REST Service and client as a whole even if not everything is required.**
              - Proposal: New API that allows for partial metadata retrieval.
              - Use Cases from Community: Only retrieving path information, Only refreshing credential
              - Ryan - Should we just force more Metadata.json cleaning to reduce size of file?
              - Hiazshou - Biggest problem is accumulation of snapshots and schema, Schema itself can be arbitrarily big. Seeing schemas >>> 100 columns. This coupled with schema evolution makes large json which cannot be cleaned.
              - Ryan - Historically metadata spec has not grown a lot
              - Yufei - Impala team just wants to know if table is updated, only needs to check path. Everytime we want a different slice of metadata.json we are creating a new endpoint at the moment. This is more difficult over time. Catalog UI usecase, only needs schema, should we make a new schema endpoint or can we have a more generic API
              - Dan - Agree with idea of maintaining metadata more. (Prior metadata location.) Most metadata that is returned is needed for most operations. Complexity of maintaining and creating new metadata requires most of the metadata. Some of this burden is on the Java implementation. Hesitant to break everything into a bunch of endpoints. Complicates building implementation. Bulk of metadata should not be large if maintained. Want to fix this first.
              - JB - Agree about maintenance as well, but just buying time. We will eventually just need more endpoints anyway. Most of time engines just need a single snapshot, discussed this a few months ago about how we may need a new endpoint just for getting the current endpoint. Maintenance helps, but may be too late in use cases with many commits.
              - Ryan - Clarifying : Proposal is for a single endpoint where you choose what is returned. We do have a way to specify a subset of snapshots coming back but we may want to change that.
                —
                It is very difficult to handle just the snapshots this way. Difficult to keep all of these things in sync. Trying to create a metadata from multiple requests that are happening differently. Leads to uncertain state (Multiple requests being unioned together)
                Want to make sure that it is actually necessary. Don’t want to add complications if getting the bundle of metadata is cheap enough.
              - Russ + Ryan - Discussed Bulk Information API vs LoadTable API for the place to put this. Russ thinks these problems are basically the same. Ryan thinks we should make a clear distinction.
              - Daniel - Wants to do Maintenance first
              - Szheon - Hive already has this
          - [Geo spec changes](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/10981)

              - Current worry may want to jettson some scope. Ryan thinks we are probably close
              - Talking about edges:
              - Szehon - We have settled on CRS and Edges. Last issue is the naming of edge naming. “Cartesian/Linear and Geodesic” vs “Planar and Spherical”
              - Bounds are “western” and “eastern” most. Call for any other comments from Geo community.
              - Jia yu - Originally had concerns about offloading CRS to table properties but are now ok. Want to offload to parquet metadata too.
              - Ryan - Are we in agreement about edge types?
              - Jia Yu - Yes, ok with compromise.
              - Martin - Waiting on comments from other experts. Geodesic alone is not quite right. Don’t want to cause confusion
              - Ryan - Isn’t edge interpretation defined by CRS?
              - Martin - No, CRS defines coordinate system. Edge defines edge interpolation.
              - Ryan - How many do we need?
              - Martin - There are a lot. Planar is the most common. Geodesic is almost the closest distance between two points. (Russ’s note I do not understand enough here to write good notes).
              - Javier - State of the industry - Planar and spherical - difference between geometry and geography. Snowflake has both as do other engines. In the future there may be more, but majority in use right now use these two. Planar and spherical are most commonly used.
              - Ryan - So most engines are using the names Planar and Spherical?
              - Javier - Yes
              - Ryan - So is there anything that is confusing about these names?
              - Martin - Yes, not that they are specific enough, they are wrong. The fact that postgres is using those names should not be sufficient to use those names.
              - Szehon - For this spec, we aren’t actually doing interpolation, we are just storing points. Shouldn’t interpolation still be up to engine? The only place where this may come in, is in our language about bounding. Since this is the only place it comes into play for Iceberg should we have this be a blocker?
              - Javier - Don’t want to get stuck on a name, but we do need to keep this data somewhere. Engines will rely on this, it should be defined by the generator.
              - Ryan - Agreed that we need to annotate. Going along with what other databases are doing is usually what we want
              - David - This is a big issue for datascience. Probability of location’s can be calculated incorrectly, this can lead to bombs getting dropped in the wrong spot. Real world consequences are very serious, defining this precisely is very important.
              - Szehon - Are the specs under defined right now? Can we have better specifications?
              - Martin - There are math terms, linear interpolation
              - David - Most folks in the community are in agreement about “Linear” and “Psuedo Geodesic”
              - Ryan - Are there any databases where linear and planar are not synonymous?
              - David -  not sure
              - Ryan - Just want to make sure we line up with engines so that terms map with what engines understand
              - David - Don’t want to add confusion to end users. When determining error on calculations have to all the way back through everything to figure it out. Want unambiguous language here.
              - Ryan - We do need to know what the generator is doing, since Iceberg don’t actually guarantee this.
              - Martin - Mapping to other systems should be possible
              - Javier - Our main users of these properties will be the engines reading the data. Lots of engines out there using this terminology already
              - Ryan - We need to figure out what engines are actually doing for these names.
              - Dewey - We have done that, just wants to use Psuedo-geodesic because “geodesic” would be wrong.
              - Ryan - What isn’t clear to me is that engines may mean the same thing by the whatever name we are using (like spherical)
              - Martin - Pseudo-geodesic has unambiguous and clear meaning
              - Ryan - So we don’t have a standard name across systems? But we think everyone is using the interpolation?
              - Not sure interpolation algorithms are the same amongst systems
              - Martin - Engines can be doing other things but that has different names
              - Daniel - So we have linear and many non-linear?
              - Martin - We can have an “unknown” interpolation option for the other set?
              - Javier - We are hitting the limits of our ability to describe things. Transferring data between engines can introduce error. Only way to really know is to get the chain of custody on how the data was generated. Even if implementations are different, Spherical is closer even if the algorithm is slightly different
              - Ryan - In spherical we have bounding box issues crossing meridians with negatives? So this is relevant for us so we do need a way to interpret non-linear interpolations and do correct math for pruning. We do want engines to annotate their edge interpolation. So maybe engines need to annotate linear / non-linear but also their edge interpolation as well.
                Bounding box calculation - Linear vs Nonlinear
                Edge Interpolation - Engine specific label, Engine should be writing this users should not be able to change this.
                We cannot be prescriptive about Edge Interpolation
              - Jia Yu - Offload Edge Interpolation to metadata.
              - Ryan - Crazy Suggestion - Should we just call Geometry and Geography. Edge interpolation just becomes engine attribution?
              - Martin - Don’t think so. Lots of different curves. There are many wrap-around problems. Issue with climatography time based wrap-around.
              - Proposal - Type Geometry, Bounding is wrap around or not. Everything else is metadata/annotation. Wrap-around needs to be determined from type but can’t be a part of edge interpolation.
              - Martin - Information is in CRS definition which is required already.
              - Ryan - Just need a flag on whether X wraps around?
              - Szehon - So we need to know which axis wrap?
              - Martin - Yes this is in CRS but we want to make it more easily accessible. Could just say every time min is > max there is a wrap around.
              - Ryan - Ok so then we don’t actually need the wrap-around parameter. How do we interpret bounding boxes in a way that we are always correct regardless of CRS?
              - Martin - for Intersection just alway flip min and max whenever min is bigger than max. Distances? No choice we need full CRS information.
              - Ryan - Engines should care about CRS since they may need to do that. We only need the ability to locate objects within bounding boxes.
              - Martin - Yes for bounding boxes no need for CRS information.
              - Ryan - OK then let’s just write up the pseudo code for that and remove the typing information. Will work with Szehon to figure this out

– Ran out of time for meeting here

  - V3

      - Variant
      - Deletion vectors and blob type
      - Row lineage
      - Defaults
      - Timestamp nanos - need reader implementations
